entry.title: How to kill a process in Linux: A cheatsheet (kill, killall, pkill, fuser)
entry.summary:
Ever had a frozen application or a rogue script that just won't die? Knowing how to properly terminate a process is a fundamental skill for any Linux user, developer, or sysadmin. This cheatsheet covers four essential commands to handle any unresponsive process: kill, killall, pkill, and the powerful fuser for network ports. This is the most precise method. First, you find the Process ID (PID), then you send a signal to it. First, find the Process ID (PID) of your app: ps aux | grep 'my_process'
Then, kill the process by its PID: kill PID_NUMBER
If it doesn't work, force kill the process: kill -9 PID_NUMBER
These commands are perfect when you don't want to look up the PID first. Kill a process by its exact name: killall my_process
Force kill a process by its exact name: killall -9 my_process
A more flexible way to kill by name (finds partial matches): pkill -f 'my_process_or_script.py'
Incredibly useful for web developers and sysadmins when a port is unexpectedly occupied. Find and kill the process using a specific port (e.g., 8443): fuser -k 8443/tcp
You can find the original PNG version of this cheatsheet in the original post: How to kill a process in Linux: A cheatsheet (kill, killall, pkill, fuser)
